//: Everything Ask AI can point at in Simple mode, the Advanced layout and the left sidebar. Ask AI's 'Show me' steps name an id; the app moves to its tab (or opens the report, folder or dialog it needs), finds the element and spotlights it. 'selector' defaults to [data-spot="<id>"]. 'item' says what the step's item names: 'match' means the element itself carries data-spot-item (a card or row); 'report', 'folder' and 'kit-review' mean the app opens that report, folder or the asset dialog for that report first. 'open' expands a collapsed section. 'page' (with 'workbook' for Sheets) is the Advanced page a 'classic' spot is on, opened first. 'layout' marks a spot that exists in one layout only ('simple', or 'classic' for Advanced); spots without it are in Simple's tabs and Settings, or in the sidebar of both layouts. Spots inside the Advanced 'Data tools' group open it first.

spots.what: The workspace switcher: the workspace the whole studio is using, with your role and layout under its name (admins switch workspaces and start a new one here)
Your role, and View as for admins: open the account menu to preview what an editor, a custom role or a channel owner sees

spots.where: Left sidebar, bottom, above your name
spots.what: The Simple | Advanced layout switch (Advanced has every tool, including research programs, sheets and scrapers)
Home: the weekly briefing: trends that need your OK, what changed, what's ready for channels, what shipped and what's running
Reports: grouped by research run, one row per trend (its Trends report and Editorial toolkit), then other reports and drafts
Trends: say Yes or Skip to new trends, then Write reports; momentum badges show which are rising or fading
Assets: a folder per research run with a folder per trend inside (its report, channel assets and pictures), Other sources, and every picture

spots.where: Left sidebar, under New and Search
spots.what: Ask AI (⌘J): in Simple it opens the Ask AI page, in Advanced the Ask AI drawer beside the page
Search (⌘K): find a report, a trend waiting for your OK, a research program or a page, or ask Ask AI what you typed
New (⌥⌘N): find new trends, a quick scan, channel assets, content from a report or a picture; admins also start a research program, invite a person or add a workspace
Collapse the sidebar to icons, or expand it again (⌘\); hover an icon to see its name
Inbox: trends that need your OK, what the channels used, edits to reports and finished or stopped runs, with an unread count
Calendar: the trends each channel plans to use, week by week, with Download .ics
Prompts: see and change the instructions behind research, reports and channel assets, with versions, a free preview and a test run
The account menu: View as (admins), My channels, Keyboard shortcuts, and Sign out in the browser studio
Analytics: which trends were approved, and which channels used them (admins only)
People & access: add people, choose their role, channel and access, and send sign-in links (admins only)
Settings (⌘,): connections, AI and pictures for the whole studio (admins only); an amber dot means Apify isn't connected

spots.where: Left sidebar, bottom (only while something runs)
spots.what: The 'N running' button: opens what's running now, each with Open and Stop
Home: what needs you this week, what changed since the last research run, and what's running
Research programs: the accounts and communities to follow, the date window, budgets and the cost estimate
Trend board: Needs your OK, Approved, Being written, Ready, with Yes / Skip and Write reports
Sheets: the Trend tracker across runs and each run's workbook
Create content: drafts from a trends report or a source brief
Library: a folder tree of research runs and their trends (Trends report, Editorial toolkit, Channel assets, Drafts, Pictures), then Other sources and the rest
Brand knowledge: audience, voice, editorial rules and approved products (admins only)
Content studio: research programs, the trend board, create content and the library, as tabs
Overview: playbooks, platform search and scrapers for collecting from the web
Data tools: opens or closes the group with Collect, Analyze, Automate and Activity
Search platforms: search Reddit, X and LinkedIn with Apify into a dataset
Scrapers: saved Apify Actors and tasks that collect into datasets
Import research: bring in a CSV, JSON or spreadsheet as a dataset
Datasets: every collected or imported dataset, with signals, conversations, topics and coverage
Dataset reports: AI reports written from one dataset (not the trends reports from research)
Compare snapshots: what changed between two datasets, and saved source checks
Ask your datasets: questions across up to eight datasets, with citations (research program posts aren't datasets yet)
Playbooks: ready-made research briefs to set up and run
Workflows: describe an outcome, preview the steps, then run them
Activity: every job and run, with logs and cancel

spots.where: Advanced, Sheets, the Trend tracker workbook (under Across runs)
spots.what: Rising, New, Steady and Fading counts across research runs; each chip filters the Trend timeline tab

Show: All, Unread, or one kind of row

Download .ics: every planned date as a calendar file for Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar
'Using, no date yet': trends a channel is using without a planned date
Every prompt, grouped (Research, Reports, Channel assets, Pictures, Assistant, Data tools, Behind every call), with search and badges: Customized · vN, Default updated, Locked
Ask AI about this prompt: explains what it does and can suggest one edit, which you apply as a new version
Edit: the prompt in order; grey parts are fixed (each says why), editable parts have value chips, live checks and Reset this block
An editable part: type here, click a value chip to insert it at the cursor; the checks under it say what's missing

spots.where: Prompts, bottom of the Edit tab (only with unsaved changes)
spots.what: Save as version N… (a note is required) or Discard
Preview: the whole prompt on a sample with your parts highlighted, and its characters, tokens and estimated cost; free
Test run…: runs this one step on the sample after you confirm the model, estimate and cap; it records a test, never a version
History: every version with who, when, where it came from (Prompts or Ask AI) and its note; compare, restore, and (admins) Lock
The People, Roles and Access log tabs
Invite people: paste work emails, choose a role (and a channel for a channel role) and, if you like, change their access
Preview as…: see the studio as any role, a channel role for one channel, or one person with their own changes
Everyone with access, with search and Role, Status, Channel and Sort filters; open a person for Details, Access (Role default, On or Off for each thing they can do), Sign-in and Activity
What each role can do: a switch per role and capability; Admin and the admin-only rows are locked, and changes save together after a review

Who changed people, roles and access, and when, in sentences; filter by person, role or kind, Load older and Download CSV
